subject: Inference footprint playbook & throughput clarifications
messages:
From: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@datacove.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-09-07T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing input: DataCove inference footprint for Q4 pilot

Marissa,

Thanks for taking this — we’re kicking off a small pilot for a recommender + chat augmentation use case and need a quick inference sizing check before our procurement window closes. I attached a short CSV with hour-by-hour qps for the last 30 days (datacove-current-traffic-snapshot.csv). High level:

- Active users: ~75k monthly active, peak hourly QPS observed: ~400
- Current traffic is spiky; expect a marketing-triggered campaign in mid-Oct that could 2–3x peaks for a few hours
- Models: mostly an open LLM (Llama-2 chat variant) plus a smaller fine-tuned 4B for quick responses

Primary asks: initial GPU count range for a Dedicated pool we should include in our internal SOW, and any obvious blockers for hitting a p95 latency of ~300–400ms.

Can we get a short checklist of exact data points you need so our infra/procurement team can turn around answers quickly? We’d like a rough budget ballpark by next Thursday.

Thanks,
Sam
Samuel Ortiz
Head of Applied ML, DataCove
Attachments: datacove-current-traffic-snapshot.csv

Subject: Re: Sizing input: DataCove inference footprint for Q4 pilot

Sam —

Appreciate the snapshot, that helps. To give a sensible Dedicated estimate we usually need a couple more data points (quick checklist below). If you can paste answers inline here we’ll run a fastback estimate and loop in engineering: 

- Expected steady-state concurrency (avg concurrent active requests) and expected burst concurrency (peak concurrent requests)
- Average prompt token length and average/95th response token length (and any max allowed)
- Desired p95 latency target and whether 300–400ms is strict or flexible for the pilot
- Typical session length and whether KV caching / long context reuse is expected
- Whether requests are single-turn or multi-turn chat sessions; if multi-turn, average number of turns and whether you need full transcript generation
- Region preference (us/eu/apac) and any data residency constraints
- Any restrictions on model variants (we can suggest quantized variants if acceptable)

If you prefer, we can run a quick online call to walk through these with your infra lead — often faster than back-and-forth email. I’ve cc’d Dev and Rishi for visibility; Dev can flag any runtime caveats.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sizing input: Sizing input: DataCove inference footprint for Q4 pilot

Looping in a few technical clarifications we typically need to produce a capacity range:

- Target p95 is critical for kernel selection: is 300ms p95 for token emission or end-to-end response?
- Batching tolerance: do you need responses streamed as tokens (low-latency) or can we batch into 50–100ms windows?
- KV cache reuse: will requests often reuse recent context (e.g., same user conversational session) — that reduces compute significantly if cache hits are high
- Model determinism & quantization tolerance: are you amenable to int8/4 quantized variants for the 4B model? That changes GPU sizing and memory footprint a lot
- Multi-model routing: do you expect Redwood to route between model sizes by route? If so, provide % traffic per model so we can mix GPU SKUs or plan subpools

If you can paste short answers to the above we’ll spin up an initial SLO-aligned deck and an ops playbook.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Inference Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@datacove.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@datacove.ai <procurement@datacove.ai>
Date: 2026-09-08T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing input: DataCove inference footprint for Q4 pilot

Hi Marissa / team — thanks, here are the clarifications (pulled from infra):

- Average concurrent active requests: ~120
- Burst concurrency (marketing-driven peaks): up to ~600 for 1–3 hours; daytime typical peaks ~300
- Average prompt tokens: 80 tokens (mostly short user queries)
- Average response tokens: 650 tokens; p95 response tokens ~1500; absolute max we might request: 2048 tokens
- Models: 70% routed to a fine-tuned 4B (fast responses), 30% routed to Llama-2-chat-13B variant for richer answers
- p95 target: end-to-end response < 350ms for the 4B path; 13B path is OK up to ~700ms
- KV cache: yes — multi-turn sessions with ~5 turns average; high reuse rate for session-level cache
- Batching tolerance: prefer streaming where possible but can accept 80–100ms micro-batching for the 13B path
- Region: us-west primarily; data residency OK in us-west cloud region
- Retention: request logs retained 30 days, embeddings persisted for 90 days

Attached an example prompt set for the pilot (example-prompt-set.txt). Can you provide a ballpark (range) of GPU SKUs and count for Dedicated? If useful we’re happy to schedule a 30-min sizing call tomorrow.

Thanks — Sam
Attachments: example-prompt-set.txt

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>

Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-09-09T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference footprint playbook & throughput clarifications

Sam — thanks for the detail, that’s exactly what we need. Quick initial thinking (rough ranges for Dedicated pool in us-west):

- 4B path (70% traffic, p95 target < 350ms): estimate 6–10 x A10G-equivalent GPUs (mixed-precision / int8 quantized) to cover steady-state concurrency 120 and sustain bursts to ~600 with autoscale buffer and short warm-up.
- 13B path (30% traffic, higher latency tolerance): estimate 2–4 x V100/A40-equivalent GPUs (or 2–3 larger A100-style SKUs) if you accept 80–100ms micro-batching and kv-cache reuse.
- If you need strict token-streaming on the 13B path (no micro-batching) increase 13B GPU count by ~50% and prefer A100-style SKUs.

Notes & next steps:
- These are first-order estimates — I’ll convert to a token/hour cost and monthly committed spend once we lock in exact batching tolerance and whether quantized variants are acceptable. See attached quick playbook (redwood-sizing-playbook-v1.pdf) for how we map tokens/concurrency to GPU SKUs.
- Dev / Priyom will run a short simulation internally (we’ll use your example prompts) and follow up with a narrow recommended pool and autoscaling policy.
- Proposed next step: 30-min sizing call Wednesday 9/10 at 10:00am PT (or Thu 9/11 1:00pm PT). Which works best?
